title: movie-planner-web viewings import/export
description: A CSV or JSON file of logged viewings — one unified row shape, all fields but title/date/medium optional, using the movie-planner CLI's own canonical field names (confirmed directly with the CLI's maintainer session, movie_planner/omdb.py as of its own #88) so a file either tool produces needs no translation to read on the other side. A plain minimal-format row (the CLI's own examples/movies.json) is just this shape with only title/date/medium/start_time/end_time/venue/imdb_url set; this app's own 'Export as JSON' additionally sets uid, start/end (full ISO instants, for exact round-trip regardless of timezone) and the OMDb-derived fields. This schema covers the JSON form only — a CSV file uses these same field names as its header row. See the bulk-import capability spec (openspec/specs/bulk-import/spec.md) for the full behaviour.

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD, interpreted in the importing visitor's own browser timezone. Required unless 'start' is present, in which case it's derived from that instant's own UTC date if omitted.

uid.description: Set only by this app's own export. When it matches an existing CalDAV entry's own uid, a re-import treats the row as a candidate update to that entry (with a per-field review before anything is written) rather than a new create. Ignored by any importer that doesn't recognise it — a new entry always gets its own freshly-minted id regardless.

start.description: Full ISO instant. Set only by this app's own export, alongside date/start_time/end_time rather than instead of them. When present, this app's own importer uses it directly instead of reconstructing the instant from date/start_time/end_time in the importing browser's own timezone.
